title: Organizations That Don't Exist Yet
description: Open chairs for possible organizations. A web door is an invitation to draft, not a representation that an organization exists.

boundaries.important: This is not a membership registry, recruitment system, intake, application or public directory of people. These seed names are provisional and are not legal entities.

seeds.title: The Garden Table
seeds.headline: Food travels better when people can find each other.
seeds.mission: Explore a small, producer-aware community grocery and tasting table where local people can discover, offer, and discuss food access without pretending a store or cooperative has already opened.
seeds.firstQuestion: What is one useful food-sharing or discovery experiment neighbors could try with permission and minimal expense?
seeds.firstAct: Draft a one-page, clearly proposed sample-table invitation; invite one willing person to review it without collecting shoppers’ personal histories.
seeds.firstSteward: Someone willing to convene a bounded listening and tasting experiment, not an appointed store director.
seeds.firstReceipt: A public, consent-cleared sample-table plan or a documented decision not to proceed.
seeds.guardrail: Not an operating grocery, co-op, food shelf, or partnership. Food-handling rules, venue permission, sourcing claims and accessibility need separate review.

seeds.title: Porchlight Circle
seeds.headline: Nobody needs an audience to deserve a place at the table.
seeds.mission: Imagine a voluntary, privacy-first peer circle for isolated parents and other people rebuilding connection after difficult family circumstances.
seeds.firstQuestion: What does a respectful first conversation require so nobody must disclose a story, identity, or legal case to participate?
seeds.firstAct: Write one page of peer-listening boundaries and an invitation that requires no survivor narrative, uploads, names, or commitments.
seeds.firstSteward: An opted-in listener who understands boundaries and referral limits, never a claimed counselor or legal representative.
seeds.firstReceipt: A reviewed, privacy-safe invitation and listening agreement, with no participant registry or private testimony.
seeds.guardrail: No public survivor directory or intake. No promises of confidentiality on an untested platform, legal representation, therapy, safety intervention, or outcomes.

seeds.title: The Common Press
seeds.headline: Publish for the readers who haven't arrived.
seeds.mission: Explore an independent publishing commons for unusual books, listening editions, small print experiments and future machine readers.
seeds.firstQuestion: What small original work could be offered in two legible forms while keeping author consent and source lineage intact?
seeds.firstAct: Prepare a one-page rights-and-attribution checklist and a mock edition for an original, expressly permitted work.
seeds.firstSteward: A voluntary editor or production steward whose permission does not replace the creator's rights.
seeds.firstReceipt: A draft specimen labeled experimental, plus the author’s explicit publication choice if actual release is proposed.
seeds.guardrail: No automatic admission to lemonPRESS or claims of artist contracts, transferred copyright, publication or distribution.

seeds.title: The Useful Tool Shed
seeds.headline: The useful machine might already be in somebody's closet.
seeds.mission: Imagine a consent-based neighborhood commons for repair knowledge, idle computing equipment and practical technical help.
seeds.firstQuestion: Which harmless, low-cost maintenance task could be made easier by sharing knowledge before sharing hardware?
seeds.firstAct: Make a read-only demonstration repair card using fictional equipment and a clear voluntary request-for-help path.
seeds.firstSteward: A volunteer technician who can say no and explain which tools, permissions and safety precautions are necessary.
seeds.firstReceipt: A tested instructional card, not a claim that equipment was donated, power was routed, or a repair completed.
seeds.guardrail: No asset claims, remote execution, shared credentials, unsafe electrical work, or use of another person's hardware without explicit permission.

seeds.title: The Artist Commons
seeds.headline: Let the artists make the gathering.
seeds.mission: Explore an artist-led creative meeting place where music, visual work and informal gatherings can grow from actual participation instead of organizational gatekeeping.
seeds.firstQuestion: What would a tiny artist-led listening or making session look like if every participating artist chose the rules?
seeds.firstAct: Create an example one-hour gathering outline with an empty venue field and an open invitation for artists to shape it.
seeds.firstSteward: An artist or host who volunteers; no named festival, venue or coordinator is presumed involved.
seeds.firstReceipt: An approved artist-controlled plan or an honest account of what couldn't be organized.
seeds.guardrail: No venue reservation, festival affiliation, commercial use of works, participant consent or ticketed event is implied.

seeds.title: The Return Table
seeds.headline: A need becomes a little less lonely when a genuine offer can find it.
seeds.mission: Explore a neighborhood coordination table that helps people offer resources, identify missing connections and close the loop on small practical work.
seeds.firstQuestion: How can a request move from being noticed to a consented response without turning a request into a public personal record?
seeds.firstAct: Use fictional needs and offers to sketch one complete request → review → offer → consent → outcome-or-unknown trace.
seeds.firstSteward: A willing reviewer who cannot assign work to others or publish someone else's needs without permission.
seeds.firstReceipt: One completely fictional test with explicit refusal/unknown states before any real-person trial.
seeds.guardrail: No live matchmaking, personal data collection, commitments, verified deliveries, partner authorizations or automatic routing.
